scope: Actual pure forwarding helper with intentionally distinct business and callback numbers; no browser/provider/network operation.

instructions.short: From your cell, dial *61*13465550142**15# and press call to send missed calls to it.
instructions.long: On AT&T: dial *61*13465550142**15# then *67*13465550142# from your business cell and press call. The first code forwards unanswered calls after 15 seconds (the **15# part sets the ring time, which keeps you under Google's 20-second clock); the second covers busy. If a code is refused, try it with two stars (**61*1...**15#). AT&T landlines use *92 and *90 instead. To turn it off later: #61# or #67# or #21#. iPhone: turn off Live Voicemail first (Settings, Phone, Live Voicemail) or it picks up before forwarding. Dial *#61# to check that forwarding is set. Test it by calling your own number from another phone and not answering; the front desk should pick up and text that phone.
instructions.offLong: To send calls back to your phone: dial #61# then #67# then #21# from your business cell. iPhone users: also check Settings, Phone, Live Voicemail is off.

instructions.short: Turn on no-answer forwarding to it in your carrier app.
instructions.long: In your phone system's admin page, set 'no answer' and 'busy' forwarding to the front desk number. The front desk number is +13465550142. Test it by calling your own number from another phone and not answering.
instructions.offLong: To send calls back to your phone, turn forwarding off in your carrier app.

finding: Current instructions do not explicitly name the saved business line and can be read as enabling forwarding on the separate callback cell.
Carrier selection does not distinguish AT&T mobile vs landline; no line-type field is collected.
The longer instruction says a test caller should be texted although phone-only service does not establish customer texting consent.
